title: H.264 compatibility checks discard profile constraints and defaults
test: tests/whep.test.js, describe 'WHEP H.264 profile-level-id matching': 'parseH264ProfileLevelId' (4 tests), 'table of offer vs router profile-level-id' (16 rows, each run as 'helper:', 'answer matcher:' and 'capability filter:' with an explicit expected match or no match), 'buildViewerRtpCapabilities H.264 entries' (6 tests: viewer fmtp instead of router parameters, level-asymmetry-allowed and numeric packetization-mode, 42e01f and mode 0 for an entry without fmtp, one entry per distinct parameter set, rtcpFeedback per entry, non-H.264 unchanged), 'against the router profiles in config.MEDIA_CODECS' (7 tests: Chrome, older Chrome, Firefox, Safari, absent profile-level-id, Baseline/Constrained High only)
proof: Before the fix, node --test tests/whep.test.js failed 46 of 112 tests, all new ones (existing tests untouched). The defect rows: an offer without profile-level-id matched a 42001f and a 640032 router codec (wildcard) in both the answer matcher and the capability filter; 42e01f matched 42001f and 640c1f matched 64001f (only the first byte, 0x42 / 0x64, was compared); 4d801f (Constrained Baseline) did not match 42e01f and 4d001f did not match 4d0032 in the capability filter; and the filtered capability carried the router's profile-level-id and level-asymmetry-allowed, never the viewer's. Output in the lane scratchpad, whep-TASK-026-before.txt. After the fix both matchers call one parsed-profile comparison (isH264Compatible: profile from profile_idc plus the profile-iop bit pattern, level ignored, packetization-mode equal with 0 as default, absent or empty profile-level-id is 42e01f, unparseable never matches) and no slice(0, 2) comparison is left in lib/whep.js. Filtered H.264 capabilities carry the viewer's profile-level-id, packetization-mode (as a number: mediasoup compares it with !== against the producer's numeric value, and the string '1' makes canConsume false, checked against the real ortc code) and level-asymmetry-allowed, one entry per distinct set. The real mediasoup ortc code (generateRouterRtpCapabilities from config.MEDIA_CODECS, getProducerRtpParametersMapping, getConsumableRtpParameters, canConsume, getConsumerRtpParameters) agrees with the WHEP filter in all ten cases tried (e.g. producer 42e01f: viewer 42e01f, no profile-level-id and 4d801f consume; viewer 42001f and packetization-mode 0 do not; producer 640032: viewer 64001f consumes, 640c1f does not; producer 4d0032: viewer 4d001f consumes). Chrome (42e01f, 42001f, 640c1f, 64001f, 4d001f) matches the router's 42e01f, 4d0032 and 640032 codecs; older Chrome 42e01f and 640032; Firefox (42e01f, 42801f) and Safari (42e01f, 640c1f) match 42e01f. npm run lint and typecheck pass; npm test passes 793 of 793. Assertion: VAL-147 (the prompt's VAL-145 is another item's id).
